vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.13

The skill bundle provides documentation for an AI agent to interface with a Gmail CLI tool ('gws') to reply to messages. The instructions in SKILL.md and metadata in _meta.json are consistent with standard productivity functionality, including support for attachments, threading, and drafts, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (replying via the gws CLI) matches the requested binary, but it defers auth and security rules to an external ../gws-shared file (or to a generator), and the package does not declare what credentials or config that shared file will require—this gap makes the package's actual runtime requirements unclear.

dimensions.detail: Name/description and the single required binary (gws) are coherent: a gmail-reply helper implemented as a thin wrapper around the gws CLI is reasonable. There are no unrelated binaries or surprising declared capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to 'Read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules' (and to run 'gws generate-skills' if missing). That delegates authentication and security behavior to an external file or a CLI generator outside this package, which is opaque here. The instructions therefore may cause the agent to create or load auth/config files or to run additional commands with broader side effects than this skill documents.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files — lowest-risk installation surface. The skill simply requires an existing gws binary on PATH.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The package declares no required environment variables or credentials, yet it refers to a shared auth document for global flags/auth. That means necessary credentials/config may be hidden in ../gws-shared/SKILL.md or produced by 'gws generate-skills' and are not declared here, so the credential footprint is unclear to reviewers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent or elevated platform privileges. There is no code that modifies other skills or system-wide settings in the provided SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a thin wrapper around the gws CLI, which is fine in principle — but before installing, inspect the referenced ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (or run the generator in a safe environment) to see exactly how authentication is handled and what credentials will be required/stored. Verify the origin and integrity of the 'gws' binary (where it came from and how it stores tokens), and prefer using --dry-run first to confirm behavior. Be cautious if the shared SKILL.md or the generator requests OAuth flows, asks to write files to global config paths, or requires unrelated service credentials. If you cannot examine gws-shared or trust the gws binary, do not install or enable the skill.
